stem: Which sequence follows the lecture’s statics method?

options.text: Unlock joints → prescribe arbitrary accelerations → call the resulting motion static equilibrium
Treat joints as locked → write each link’s force/moment balance → project the required effort onto each joint axis
Project joint efforts → integrate acceleration → replace all link balances with velocity propagation
Write only force balance → ignore moments → infer effort from link length alone

citations.locator: Lecture 10, physical PDF page 338, printed slide 13: displayed derivation, text and associated figure
citations.evidenceText:
Static Forces in Manipulators

•  When manipulator act on environment, what
   should be the joint torques that must be acting to
   keep the system in static equilibrium?
•  Method
     1.  First, lock all the joints so that the manipulator
      becomes a structure.
     2. Consider each link in this structure and write a
      force/moment balance relationship in terms of
       the link frames.
     3.  Finally, compute what static torque must be
        acting about the joint axis in order for the
       manipulator to be in static equilibrium.


                                                                                                          13

solution.justification: Static equilibrium is determined from force and moment balance, then the actuator component along the joint freedom is extracted.

optionExplanations.choice-2: Acceleration integration is not this static procedure.
optionExplanations.choice-3: Moment balance is essential for torque.
optionExplanations.choice-4: Nonzero arbitrary acceleration contradicts the stated static condition.

   – Based on conservation of energy.
